stops.note: a rampart of stakes and earth; Hadrian's Wall, begun in AD 122, has a great earthwork behind it that archaeologists call the Vallum
the Old English poem The Ruin marvels at crumbling Roman walls, probably those of Bath, as 'the work of giants'
kept the sense of a built stone barrier; 'the writing on the wall' comes from Belshazzar's feast in the Book of Daniel

current_meaning: a continuous upright structure enclosing or dividing an area
